page: Microsoft Azure FX64mds_v2 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the FXmdsv2 family, designed for memory-intensive workloads. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The processor includes 260 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The server is equipped with 1344.0 GB of RAM, providing 21.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage consists of a 3780 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance operates under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results show strong multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 70926.61 and a PassMark CPU score of 85402.59. Memory performance is notable, with uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching a top-tier 392.4 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 170.98 GB/sec, though the PassMark memory score sits in the average category at 2663.42. The server demonstrates top-tier efficiency in database operations, scoring 37190.82 on PassMark database tests, and achieves a static web serving throughput of 97.07 GB/sec. For AI workloads, the hardware processes 7B parameter LLM prompts at 292.5 tokens/sec and generates text at 33.1 tokens/sec.

From a resource density perspective, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and integrated NVMe storage provide high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound applications, reducing the need to scale out to larger instances merely for RAM capacity. However, single-core performance represents a relative tradeoff, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring in the average tier. This server is suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data warehousing, and memory-heavy enterprise applications.
